newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Buenos Aires province to sell utilities, railroad.
newsitem.headline: Buenos Aires province to sell utilities, railroad.

text.p: The Argentine province of Buenos Aires on Tuesday said it would privatize its railroad network and two electric utilities valued at $1.4 billion.

Hugo Toledo, the province's public works and services minister, said the proposed sale of Empresa Social de Energia de Buenos Aires SA (ESEBA) has attracted the interest of 21 Argentine and foreign companies.
"It is beyond the most optimistic projections of those of us who traveled the world pointing out the virtues of the firm," he told foreign correspondents.

Among those who paid $35,000 for the tender specifications are Argentina's YPF SA, Compania Naviera Prez Companc, Central Costanera SA and Sideco, a subsidiary of SOCMA, an industrial group controlled by the Macri family. Others requesting the specifications were Chile's Enersis SA, Chilquinta SA and Sociedad Austral de Electricidad SA, Spain's Iberdrola and Italy's Camuzzi.
Credit Suisse First Boston is the adviser in the sale.

The minister refused to disclose the minimum price set for ESEBA, though Buenos Aires Governor Eduardo Duhalde has said he expects the utility to fetch more than $1 billion. Duhalde has also said he expects to reap $400 million for a 30-year concession for Obras Sanitarias de Buenos Aires, a water and sewage company.
Buenos Aires is also well advanced in its plans to award a 29-year concession this year to operate provincial railroads, Toledo said. He did not reveal the base price.

ESEBA generates, distributes and transports electricity in an area as large as Spain. Its territory is inhabited by 13 million people and generates about 40 percent of Argentina's gross domestic product.
The generation sector of the company will be sold while the distribution and transport areas will be awarded in a 95-year concession, Toledo said.
The company turned a $50 million deficit in 1995 into a $200,000 surplus last year. It expects to break even this year, ESEBA President Jos Romero said on Tuesday.
